Design Language Atlas

Visual traditions from art, craft, architecture and graphic design, with a deep section on Türkiye and Anatolia. Each entry has its feel, its materials, four colours, and names to look up next.

Eight hand-picked favourites to start with: shadow and light, wood, quiet restraint and deep colour. Pick one to jump straight to it.

  • Türkiye & Anatolia · c. 9600–6000 BCE

    Göbekli Tepe & Neolithic Anatolia

    The oldest monumental art on earth: T-shaped stone pillars carved with foxes, boars and vultures.

    Limestone, low relief, rings of pillars, ochre wall paintings at Çatalhöyük.

    Look up: Göbekli Tepe pillars, Çatalhöyük murals, Karahan Tepe

    WikipediaImages

  • Türkiye & Anatolia · c. 1600–1180 BCE

    Hittite relief

    Processions of gods cut into living rock, heavy and certain.

    Basalt and rock-face relief, sun discs, lions, bronze standards.

    Look up: Yazılıkaya, Alaca Höyük sun discs, Lion Gate at Hattusa

    WikipediaImages

  • Türkiye & Anatolia · c. 500–1450

    Byzantine mosaic

    Gold tesserae that glitter in candlelight; flat, frontal, sacred figures.

    Gold ground, glass tesserae, deep blues and purples, light that moves as you walk.

    Look up: Hagia Sophia mosaics, Chora (Kariye) mosaics, Ravenna

    WikipediaImages

  • Türkiye & Anatolia · c. 300–1200

    Cappadocian rock-cut

    Rooms carved into soft volcanic rock and painted in the dark.

    Tuff stone, cave interiors, small openings, frescoes in ochre and blue.

    Look up: Göreme Open Air Museum, Dark Church, Derinkuyu

    WikipediaImages

  • Türkiye & Anatolia · 12th–13th c.

    Seljuk stone geometry

    Austere stone buildings with explosive carved portals.

    Cut stone, deep relief, star polygons, muqarnas, turquoise and black tile inside.

    Look up: Divriği Great Mosque, Sivas Gök Medrese, Karatay Medrese, Sultanhanı

    WikipediaImages

  • Türkiye & Anatolia · c. 1480–1620

    İznik çini

    The Ottoman flower garden in glazed tile: tulips, carnations, saz leaves.

    Look up: Rüstem Paşa Mosque, Topkapı Circumcision Room

    WikipediaImages

  • Türkiye & Anatolia · 16th c.

    Saz style

    Ink drawings of long serrated leaves swirling around dragons and birds.

    Fine line, movement, hybrid creatures, often black ink alone.

    Look up: Şahkulu, saz yolu drawings, Topkapı albums

    WikipediaImages

  • Türkiye & Anatolia · 15th–20th c.

    Hat: Ottoman calligraphy

    Writing treated like architecture: letters stacked and balanced like a building.

    Thuluth and celî scripts, istif compositions, burnished paper, black and gold.

  • Türkiye & Anatolia · 14th–19th c.

    Tuğra
